verdict.rationale: Cerebras documents first-party automatic prompt caching that needs no code changes. It also documents that cached tokens don't count toward the uncached TPM limit, which raises effective throughput on repeated context. However, the pack never says caching lowers latency (e.g., TTFT) or price per cached token, so the story's latency-or-cost benefit is only implied. missing for 10: documented latency/TTFT reduction from cache hits, documented cached-token pricing discount, details on supported models and cache scope or lifetime, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can benefit from prompt/prefix caching that reduces latency or cost on repeated context

citations.quote: Cerebras Prompt Caching works automatically on all supported API requests. No code changes are required.
Cached tokens don't count toward your uncached TPM limit, so a higher cache hit rate lets you process far more total tokens within the same uncached limit.
Improving your cache hit rate lets the same uncached limit serve significantly more total tokens
